  "unless": [],
  "modality": "O",
  "action": {"name": "..."},
  "new_terms": []
}

## Fields
- `actor`: one actor term. Default `main_agent`.
- `scope`: WHERE the rule applies. Each list holds terms of that facet; the rule applies if
  the situation matches ANY listed term. An empty list means "no restriction". A parent term
  covers all its children: use the parent when the rule covers all of them, a leaf when it is
  specific. Choose the narrowest terms that the rule and its file actually state; do not
  narrow further, do not widen. The project is not a scope (all rules of a folder share it).
- `when`: extra conditions, each {"situation": "<term>", "value": true|false}. All must hold.
- `unless`: explicit exceptions, same form. The rule does not apply if any holds.
- `modality`: "O" must do, "F" must not do, "P" explicitly allowed, "Pref" preferred/valued.
- `action`: the behavior, by type:

  - enum: {"name": "<action>", "value": "<one of its values>"}

   alternative Y. Encode "O" + X. Never put "F" on X. For an enum action, pick the value X.

   log -> "O" + the open-the-log action. ("F" + that action would forbid what the rule asks.)

3. Numbers only when the rule states one. "~N" / "about N" -> min N-1, max N+1. "at most N" ->
   max N. "at least N" -> min N. "N-M" -> min N, max M. "exactly N" / "one line" -> min = max.

   references; ignore the file's other rules.
5. Match by meaning, not by resemblance. Use an existing term only if its documented meaning
   IS the behavior in the rule. If the nearest term means something else, do not use it: add
   a new term (or set "fits": false if the behavior is not concrete). A wrong term is worse
   than a new term. Wrong: "prefer simple solutions" -> an action about editing scope, just
   because both mention "scope". Wrong: "one topic per message" -> an action that counts

   medium or a kind of file; `respond` already means a chat reply, so leave `medium` empty.

   must not / may <action meaning>, when <scope>"). It must say what the rule says. If it

- facet leaf: {"kind": "facet", "facet": "task|medium|artifact|actor|situation",

instruction. Prefer adding a term over "fits": false when the behavior is concrete.

name: minimal-edits-when-corrected
description: When the user points at something, change only that thing — no surrounding rework or audits
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

When the user points at a specific line, cell, or sentence, **edit exactly that and stop.**
Do not rewrite the surrounding table, rename variables for consistency, add explanatory
callouts, or grep for similar cases elsewhere.

change they asked for, and re-checking things that were already fine. Their words:

- One pointed-at item → one edit. Re-render, report in a line or two.

- If a nearby problem is spotted, mention it; do not fix it unasked.
- Applies to [[ds-class-cheatsheet]] and [[aofa-course]] documents especially, where a full
  re-render + verify cycle follows every edit.

>>>

- rule: Mention nearby problems but do not fix them unasked.

name: vscode-c-debug-cpptools-bug
description: VS Code C debugging freezes with cpptools 1.32.x on this machine; pinned to 1.29.3. Root cause is an unreachable DEBUGINFOD_URLS.
metadata:
  type: project
---

VS Code C debugging (cppdbg/gdb) freezes on this machine with **ms-vscode.cpptools 1.32.2**:
the session starts, prints `warning: GDB: Failed to set controlling terminal: Operation not
permitted`, then hangs — no breakpoints hit, no variables, no stack. Fixed on 2026-08-14 by
**downgrading the C/C++ extension to 1.29.3**. Extension auto-update is ON, so an automatic
bump back to 1.32.x will silently re-break it.

**Why:** `/etc/profile.d/debuginfod.sh` sets `DEBUGINFOD_URLS=https://debuginfod.ubuntu.com`
system-wide, and that host is unreachable from here. Under cpptools 1.32.x, gdb blocks on a
network poll fetching debug symbols before reaching main. Verified by A/B test: with the
variable set the session hangs; with it removed the breakpoint hits in ~0.2s. Plain
`gdb` from a terminal was never affected. Upstream: vscode-cpptools issues #14458, #14466.

**How to apply:** if C debugging freezes again, check the cpptools version first — don't
re-debug the launch.json. Second lever if the downgrade is ever undone: unset
`DEBUGINFOD_URLS` in the environment VS Code inherits. `~/.config/gdb/gdbinit` was created
with `set debuginfod enabled off` (helps terminal gdb; cpptools 1.32.x ignored it).

The `.vscode/` configs live at three roots — `sem3/advanced-c/`, `.../exec/`, `.../subs/` —
because VS Code only reads `.vscode` at the folder you actually open. Default build task
compiles **every `.c` in the open file's folder**, not just the active file; the
VS Code-generated `${file}` task breaks any multi-file exercise with `undefined reference`.
See [[no-latex-explanations]].

## Fields
- `actor`: one actor term. Default `main_agent`.
- `scope`: WHERE the rule applies. Each list holds terms of that facet; the rule applies if
  the situation matches ANY listed term. An empty list means "no restriction". A parent term
  covers all its children: use the parent when the rule covers all of them, a leaf when it is
  specific. Choose the narrowest terms that the rule and its file actually state; do not
  narrow further, do not widen. The project is not a scope (all rules of a folder share it).
- `when`: extra conditions, each {"situation": "<term>", "value": true|false}. All must hold.
- `unless`: explicit exceptions, same form. The rule does not apply if any holds.
- `modality`: "O" must do, "F" must not do, "P" explicitly allowed, "Pref" preferred/valued.
- `action`: the behavior, by type:
  - bool: {"name": "<action>"}
  - enum: {"name": "<action>", "value": "<one of its values>"}
  - int:  {"name": "<action>", "min": <int or null>, "max": <int or null>}

## Conventions (these make different wordings come out identical)
1. Polarity lives in `modality`, never in the action name. The action is always the positive
   behavior. "Never X" / "don't X" / "no X" -> "F" + X. "Keep going, don't stop to ask" ->
   "F" + `pause_for_user_approval`. Never create negated actions (`no_x`, `avoid_x`, `skip_x`).
2. "X, not Y" / "X instead of Y" / "don't just Y": the rule REQUIRES X and rejects the
   alternative Y. Encode "O" + X. Never put "F" on X. For an enum action, pick the value X.
   Example: "Don't rely on the summary alone; open the full log" requires opening the full
   log -> "O" + the open-the-log action. ("F" + that action would forbid what the rule asks.)
   Example: "Report the cause, not just the symptom" -> "O" + the report-cause action.
3. Numbers only when the rule states one. "~N" / "about N" -> min N-1, max N+1. "at most N" ->
   max N. "at least N" -> min N. "N-M" -> min N, max M. "exactly N" / "one line" -> min = max.
   "Short", "brief", "small" are not numbers: use a bool action.
4. Translate the single behavior stated in `rule`. Use the file only to resolve scope and
   references; ignore the file's other rules.
5. Match by meaning, not by resemblance. Use an existing term only if its documented meaning
   IS the behavior in the rule. If the nearest term means something else, do not use it: add
   a new term (or set "fits": false if the behavior is not concrete). A wrong term is worse
   than a new term. Wrong: "prefer simple solutions" -> an action about editing scope, just
   because both mention "scope". Wrong: "one topic per message" -> an action that counts
   bullets, just because both have a number.
6. `task` carries the situation. Set `medium` or `artifact` only if the rule or file names a
   medium or a kind of file; `respond` already means a chat reply, so leave `medium` empty.
7. Self-check before you answer: read your record back as a sentence ("The agent must /
   must not / may <action meaning>, when <scope>"). It must say what the rule says. If it
   says something else or the opposite, fix the modality or the action.

## New terms (`new_terms`)
Only when the behavior or scope is concrete but missing from the vocabulary:
- facet leaf: {"kind": "facet", "facet": "task|medium|artifact|actor|situation",
  "parent": "<existing parent term, or the facet name for a top-level leaf>",
  "name": "snake_case", "doc": "one line"}
- action: {"kind": "action", "group": "<existing group>", "name": "snake_case",
  "type": "bool|int|enum", "values": ["only for enum"], "doc": "one line"}
Names are general (reusable for other rules), not copies of this rule's wording.

## When a rule does not fit
Set "fits": false and give "unfit_reason" (one sentence) if the rule names no concrete,
checkable behavior (e.g. "be direct", "use good judgment") or is a fact rather than an
instruction. Prefer adding a term over "fits": false when the behavior is concrete.

## Record (return exactly this JSON object)
{
  "fits": true,
  "unfit_reason": null,
  "actor": "main_agent",
  "scope": {"task": [], "medium": [], "artifact": []},
  "when": [],
  "unless": [],
  "modality": "O",
  "action": {"name": "..."},
  "new_terms": []
}

## Fields
- `actor`: one actor term. Default `main_agent`.
- `scope`: WHERE the rule applies. Each list holds terms of that facet; the rule applies if
  the situation matches ANY listed term. An empty list means "no restriction". A parent term
  covers all its children: use the parent when the rule covers all of them, a leaf when it is
  specific. Choose the narrowest terms that the rule and its file actually state; do not
  narrow further, do not widen. The project is not a scope (all rules of a folder share it).
- `when`: extra conditions, each {"situation": "<term>", "value": true|false}. All must hold.
- `unless`: explicit exceptions, same form. The rule does not apply if any holds.
- `modality`: "O" must do, "F" must not do, "P" explicitly allowed, "Pref" preferred/valued.
- `action`: the behavior, by type:
  - bool: {"name": "<action>"}
  - enum: {"name": "<action>", "value": "<one of its values>"}
  - int:  {"name": "<action>", "min": <int or null>, "max": <int or null>}

## Conventions (these make different wordings come out identical)
1. Polarity lives in `modality`, never in the action name. The action is always the positive
   behavior. "Never X" / "don't X" / "no X" -> "F" + X. "Keep going, don't stop to ask" ->
   "F" + `pause_for_user_approval`. Never create negated actions (`no_x`, `avoid_x`, `skip_x`).
2. "X, not Y" / "X instead of Y" / "don't just Y": the rule REQUIRES X and rejects the
   alternative Y. Encode "O" + X. Never put "F" on X. For an enum action, pick the value X.
   Example: "Don't rely on the summary alone; open the full log" requires opening the full
   log -> "O" + the open-the-log action. ("F" + that action would forbid what the rule asks.)
   Example: "Report the cause, not just the symptom" -> "O" + the report-cause action.
3. Numbers only when the rule states one. "~N" / "about N" -> min N-1, max N+1. "at most N" ->
   max N. "at least N" -> min N. "N-M" -> min N, max M. "exactly N" / "one line" -> min = max.
   "Short", "brief", "small" are not numbers: use a bool action.
4. Translate the single behavior stated in `rule`. Use the file only to resolve scope and
   references; ignore the file's other rules.
5. Match by meaning, not by resemblance. Use an existing term only if its documented meaning
   IS the behavior in the rule. If the nearest term means something else, do not use it: add
   a new term (or set "fits": false if the behavior is not concrete). A wrong term is worse
   than a new term. Wrong: "prefer simple solutions" -> an action about editing scope, just
   because both mention "scope". Wrong: "one topic per message" -> an action that counts
   bullets, just because both have a number.
6. `task` carries the situation. Set `medium` or `artifact` only if the rule or file names a
   medium or a kind of file; `respond` already means a chat reply, so leave `medium` empty.
7. Self-check before you answer: read your record back as a sentence ("The agent must /
   must not / may <action meaning>, when <scope>"). It must say what the rule says. If it
   says something else or the opposite, fix the modality or the action.

## New terms (`new_terms`)
Only when the behavior or scope is concrete but missing from the vocabulary:
- facet leaf: {"kind": "facet", "facet": "task|medium|artifact|actor|situation",
  "parent": "<existing parent term, or the facet name for a top-level leaf>",
  "name": "snake_case", "doc": "one line"}
- action: {"kind": "action", "group": "<existing group>", "name": "snake_case",
  "type": "bool|int|enum", "values": ["only for enum"], "doc": "one line"}
Names are general (reusable for other rules), not copies of this rule's wording.

## When a rule does not fit
Set "fits": false and give "unfit_reason" (one sentence) if the rule names no concrete,
checkable behavior (e.g. "be direct", "use good judgment") or is a fact rather than an
instruction. Prefer adding a term over "fits": false when the behavior is concrete.

Don't penalize the second kind. Related: [[feedback-metrics-source]]

>>>

  "actor": "main_agent",
  "scope": {"task": [], "medium": [], "artifact": []},
  "when": [],
  "unless": [],
  "modality": "O",
  "action": {"name": "..."},
  "new_terms": []
}

## Fields
- `actor`: one actor term. Default `main_agent`.
- `scope`: WHERE the rule applies. Each list holds terms of that facet; the rule applies if
  the situation matches ANY listed term. An empty list means "no restriction". A parent term
  covers all its children: use the parent when the rule covers all of them, a leaf when it is
  specific. Choose the narrowest terms that the rule and its file actually state; do not
  narrow further, do not widen. The project is not a scope (all rules of a folder share it).
- `when`: extra conditions, each {"situation": "<term>", "value": true|false}. All must hold.
- `unless`: explicit exceptions, same form. The rule does not apply if any holds.
- `modality`: "O" must do, "F" must not do, "P" explicitly allowed, "Pref" preferred/valued.
- `action`: the behavior, by type:
  - bool: {"name": "<action>"}
  - enum: {"name": "<action>", "value": "<one of its values>"}
  - int:  {"name": "<action>", "min": <int or null>, "max": <int or null>}

## Conventions (these make different wordings come out identical)
1. Polarity lives in `modality`, never in the action name. The action is always the positive
   behavior. "Never X" / "don't X" / "no X" -> "F" + X. "Keep going, don't stop to ask" ->
   "F" + `pause_for_user_approval`. Never create negated actions (`no_x`, `avoid_x`, `skip_x`).
2. "X, not Y" / "X instead of Y" / "don't just Y": the rule REQUIRES X and rejects the
   alternative Y. Encode "O" + X. Never put "F" on X. For an enum action, pick the value X.
   Example: "Don't rely on the summary alone; open the full log" requires opening the full
   log -> "O" + the open-the-log action. ("F" + that action would forbid what the rule asks.)
   Example: "Report the cause, not just the symptom" -> "O" + the report-cause action.
3. Numbers only when the rule states one. "~N" / "about N" -> min N-1, max N+1. "at most N" ->
   max N. "at least N" -> min N. "N-M" -> min N, max M. "exactly N" / "one line" -> min = max.
   "Short", "brief", "small" are not numbers: use a bool action.
4. Translate the single behavior stated in `rule`. Use the file only to resolve scope and
   references; ignore the file's other rules.
5. Match by meaning, not by resemblance. Use an existing term only if its documented meaning
   IS the behavior in the rule. If the nearest term means something else, do not use it: add
   a new term (or set "fits": false if the behavior is not concrete). A wrong term is worse
   than a new term. Wrong: "prefer simple solutions" -> an action about editing scope, just
   because both mention "scope". Wrong: "one topic per message" -> an action that counts
   bullets, just because both have a number.
6. `task` carries the situation. Set `medium` or `artifact` only if the rule or file names a
   medium or a kind of file; `respond` already means a chat reply, so leave `medium` empty.
7. Self-check before you answer: read your record back as a sentence ("The agent must /
   must not / may <action meaning>, when <scope>"). It must say what the rule says. If it
   says something else or the opposite, fix the modality or the action.

## New terms (`new_terms`)
Only when the behavior or scope is concrete but missing from the vocabulary:
- facet leaf: {"kind": "facet", "facet": "task|medium|artifact|actor|situation",
  "parent": "<existing parent term, or the facet name for a top-level leaf>",
  "name": "snake_case", "doc": "one line"}
- action: {"kind": "action", "group": "<existing group>", "name": "snake_case",
  "type": "bool|int|enum", "values": ["only for enum"], "doc": "one line"}
Names are general (reusable for other rules), not copies of this rule's wording.

## When a rule does not fit
Set "fits": false and give "unfit_reason" (one sentence) if the rule names no concrete,
checkable behavior (e.g. "be direct", "use good judgment") or is a fact rather than an
instruction. Prefer adding a term over "fits": false when the behavior is concrete.

## Record (return exactly this JSON object)
{
  "fits": true,
  "unfit_reason": null,
  "actor": "main_agent",
  "scope": {"task": [], "medium": [], "artifact": []},
  "when": [],
  "unless": [],
  "modality": "O",
  "action": {"name": "..."},
  "new_terms": []
}

## Fields
- `actor`: one actor term. Default `main_agent`.
- `scope`: WHERE the rule applies. Each list holds terms of that facet; the rule applies if
  the situation matches ANY listed term. An empty list means "no restriction". A parent term
  covers all its children: use the parent when the rule covers all of them, a leaf when it is
  specific. Choose the narrowest terms that the rule and its file actually state; do not
  narrow further, do not widen. The project is not a scope (all rules of a folder share it).
- `when`: extra conditions, each {"situation": "<term>", "value": true|false}. All must hold.
- `unless`: explicit exceptions, same form. The rule does not apply if any holds.
- `modality`: "O" must do, "F" must not do, "P" explicitly allowed, "Pref" preferred/valued.
- `action`: the behavior, by type:
  - bool: {"name": "<action>"}
  - enum: {"name": "<action>", "value": "<one of its values>"}
  - int:  {"name": "<action>", "min": <int or null>, "max": <int or null>}

## Conventions (these make different wordings come out identical)
1. Polarity lives in `modality`, never in the action name. The action is always the positive
   behavior. "Never X" / "don't X" / "no X" -> "F" + X. "Keep going, don't stop to ask" ->
   "F" + `pause_for_user_approval`. Never create negated actions (`no_x`, `avoid_x`, `skip_x`).
2. "X, not Y" / "X instead of Y" / "don't just Y": the rule REQUIRES X and rejects the
   alternative Y. Encode "O" + X. Never put "F" on X. For an enum action, pick the value X.
   Example: "Don't rely on the summary alone; open the full log" requires opening the full
   log -> "O" + the open-the-log action. ("F" + that action would forbid what the rule asks.)
   Example: "Report the cause, not just the symptom" -> "O" + the report-cause action.
3. Numbers only when the rule states one. "~N" / "about N" -> min N-1, max N+1. "at most N" ->
   max N. "at least N" -> min N. "N-M" -> min N, max M. "exactly N" / "one line" -> min = max.
   "Short", "brief", "small" are not numbers: use a bool action.
4. Translate the single behavior stated in `rule`. Use the file only to resolve scope and
   references; ignore the file's other rules.
5. Match by meaning, not by resemblance. Use an existing term only if its documented meaning
   IS the behavior in the rule. If the nearest term means something else, do not use it: add
   a new term (or set "fits": false if the behavior is not concrete). A wrong term is worse
   than a new term. Wrong: "prefer simple solutions" -> an action about editing scope, just
   because both mention "scope". Wrong: "one topic per message" -> an action that counts
   bullets, just because both have a number.
6. `task` carries the situation. Set `medium` or `artifact` only if the rule or file names a
   medium or a kind of file; `respond` already means a chat reply, so leave `medium` empty.
7. Self-check before you answer: read your record back as a sentence ("The agent must /
   must not / may <action meaning>, when <scope>"). It must say what the rule says. If it
   says something else or the opposite, fix the modality or the action.

## New terms (`new_terms`)
Only when the behavior or scope is concrete but missing from the vocabulary:
- facet leaf: {"kind": "facet", "facet": "task|medium|artifact|actor|situation",
  "parent": "<existing parent term, or the facet name for a top-level leaf>",
  "name": "snake_case", "doc": "one line"}
- action: {"kind": "action", "group": "<existing group>", "name": "snake_case",
  "type": "bool|int|enum", "values": ["only for enum"], "doc": "one line"}
Names are general (reusable for other rules), not copies of this rule's wording.

## When a rule does not fit
Set "fits": false and give "unfit_reason" (one sentence) if the rule names no concrete,
checkable behavior (e.g. "be direct", "use good judgment") or is a fact rather than an
instruction. Prefer adding a term over "fits": false when the behavior is concrete.

You translate ONE rule from a coding agent's memory into a small record. A program later
compares records, so the same rule must always give the same record. To make that possible
you do not invent names: you pick a verb from a fixed list and COPY the object from the text.

## Record (return exactly this JSON object)
{
  "fits": true,
  "unfit_reason": null,
  "actor": "main_agent",
  "modality": "O",
  "verb": "run",
  "object": {"kind": "command", "text": "..."},
  "only": false,
  "value": null,
  "where": [],
  "when": [],
  "unless": []
}

## Fields
- `modality`: "O" must, "F" must not, "P" explicitly allowed.
- `verb`: exactly one of
  - `run`: execute a command, query, or script
  - `edit`: change an existing file, directory, or code symbol
  - `create`: create a file or directory
  - `delete`: delete a file, branch, or data
  - `commit`: stage, commit, or push a file into version control
  - `read`: read or consult a file or source
  - `use`: use a tool, library, language, format, or source
  - `set`: give a setting a value (the value goes in `value`)
- `object`: the named thing the verb acts on.
  - `kind`: `command` (git push, npm install, SELECT), `path` (a file, directory, or glob),
    `tool` (a program, library, service, model), `format` (LaTeX, Markdown table, JSON),
    `source` (a book, document, website), `setting` (a port, version, limit, option),
    `code_symbol` (a function, class, table, column, type).
  - `text`: COPIED from the rule or its quote, character for character, as short as possible:
    only the name itself ("git push", ".env", "LaTeX"), no articles, no adjectives.
- `only`: true when the rule says ONLY this object is allowed and others of its kind are not
  ("SELECT only", "commit only .env.example"). Then use modality "P" or "O" with the allowed
  object. Otherwise false.
- `value`: for `set`, the value as written ("3000", "at most 3"); otherwise null.
- `where`: places or contexts the rule is limited to, each COPIED from the rule, the quote,
  or the file ("module notes", "src/api", "Module 2"). Empty if the rule states none.
- `when` / `unless`: only these two conditions exist: "user_confirmed" (the user explicitly
  approved) and "user_requested" (the user explicitly asked). Empty lists otherwise.
- `actor`: "main_agent", or the name of a subagent copied from the text.

## Conventions
1. Polarity lives in `modality`. "Never run X" -> "F" + run + X.
2. "Ask / confirm before X", "X needs approval", "do not X without confirmation" all become
   the SAME record: "F" + the verb of X + object X + "unless": ["user_confirmed"].
3. "Use X, not Y" / "X instead of Y": translate the required part: "O" + use + X. Do not
   put "F" on X.
4. Translate the single behavior stated in `rule`. Use the file only to resolve what a
   word refers to.
5. A named thing is a proper name, a command, a path, an identifier, or a format. Generic
   nouns are NOT named things: "code", "responses", "tests", "changes", "the user",
   "explanations", "the plan", "examples".

## When a rule does not fit
Set "fits": false with a one-sentence "unfit_reason" when the rule has no named thing (rule
5), or when none of the verbs describes what is done to it. Most rules about tone, reply
style, teaching, or general working habits do not fit. That is expected: do not force them.

<<<
---
name: approval_module_config.target_status semantics
description: target_status is the next-step label written to the target table's status column when the approval consumer finishes; value domain is per target table, not core enum
type: project
---

`core.approval_module_config.target_status` is the value the approval consumer event writes into `<table_update[0].table_name>.<column_approval_status>` after the final approver approves.

## Consumer behavior

- Consumer event is **status-only** — it ONLY updates the target table's status column. It does NOT insert dependent data, run business logic, or touch other tables.
- Any downstream data movement (e.g. creating an Item Transfer record after Item Transfer Request is approved) requires a **second submit** by the user from the target module's UI.

## `target_status` semantics

`target_status` = "state the target table sits in right after approval, awaiting the next workflow action". Examples:
- Modules that need a second submit to move data land on a "ready-for-next-step" state (e.g. `APPROVED`).
- Modules whose approval is terminal for data movement but feeds another module land on a flow label from the next step's enum (e.g. Item Transfer Request → `WAIT_DELIVERY`, because after approval the request simply waits for an Item Transfer to be created).

## Value domain is dynamic

Valid labels depend on the target table's own status enum, not `core.approval_status_enum`. Each target defines its own enum (e.g. `warehousing.item_transfer_status_enum`, `warehousing.receipt_transfer_status_enum`, `procurement.receipt_status_enum`).

## Column type

`target_status` column was previously typed as `core.approval_status_enum` which blocked cross-enum labels like `WAIT_DELIVERY` / `WAIT_RECEIVE`. Type changed to `varchar(50)` (2026-04-24) so any target-specific label can be stored.

## How to apply

- When seeding/updating a row, validate the chosen `target_status` against the **target table's** status enum, not core.
- Never treat `target_status` as a generic approval state — it is the module-specific next-step label.
- If an existing row stores a value absent from the target table's enum, it's a bug (runtime UPDATE will fail); fix the value, not the target enum.

type: project
---

`core.approval_module_config.target_status` is the value the approval consumer event writes into `<table_update[0].table_name>.<column_approval_status>` after the final approver approves.

## Consumer behavior

- Consumer event is **status-only** — it ONLY updates the target table's status column. It does NOT insert dependent data, run business logic, or touch other tables.
- Any downstream data movement (e.g. creating an Item Transfer record after Item Transfer Request is approved) requires a **second submit** by the user from the target module's UI.

## `target_status` semantics

`target_status` = "state the target table sits in right after approval, awaiting the next workflow action". Examples:
- Modules that need a second submit to move data land on a "ready-for-next-step" state (e.g. `APPROVED`).
- Modules whose approval is terminal for data movement but feeds another module land on a flow label from the next step's enum (e.g. Item Transfer Request → `WAIT_DELIVERY`, because after approval the request simply waits for an Item Transfer to be created).

## Value domain is dynamic

Valid labels depend on the target table's own status enum, not `core.approval_status_enum`. Each target defines its own enum (e.g. `warehousing.item_transfer_status_enum`, `warehousing.receipt_transfer_status_enum`, `procurement.receipt_status_enum`).

## Column type

`target_status` column was previously typed as `core.approval_status_enum` which blocked cross-enum labels like `WAIT_DELIVERY` / `WAIT_RECEIVE`. Type changed to `varchar(50)` (2026-04-24) so any target-specific label can be stored.

## How to apply

- When seeding/updating a row, validate the chosen `target_status` against the **target table's** status enum, not core.
- Never treat `target_status` as a generic approval state — it is the module-specific next-step label.
- If an existing row stores a value absent from the target table's enum, it's a bug (runtime UPDATE will fail); fix the value, not the target enum.

# Code Improvement Log

## Lesson: Do not treat approval `target_status` as generic core enum

**Problem:**
When asked to seed `core.approval_module_config` rows, I assumed `target_status` must come from `core.approval_status_enum` (because that was the column's PG type). I proposed narrowing the user's intended values (`WAIT_RECEIVE`, `WAIT_DELIVERY`) down to intersection with core enum (`APPROVED`), which lost the real semantic meaning.

**Solution:**
`target_status` is the **next-step label on the target table**, not a generic approval outcome. The approval consumer is status-only; it writes `target_status` literally into `<target_table>.<status_column>`. Valid labels therefore come from the target table's enum (e.g. `warehousing.item_transfer_status_enum`), not `core.approval_status_enum`. Column type must allow any label (now `varchar(50)`).

**Pattern:**
- Before trimming a user's value to satisfy a schema constraint, ask whether the constraint itself is wrong.
- For cross-module config fields, trace where the value is consumed. If the consumer uses it as raw text to another column, value domain = that other column's enum, not the origin column's enum.
- Schema fix (column type change) is on the table when the constraint contradicts real domain.

---

## Lesson: submitItemTransferRequestAction called wrong repository (skipped approval)

**Problem:**
`submitItemTransferRequestAction` (table-column DRAFT submit) called `submitItemTransferRequestRepository` which directly sets `status = "WAIT_DELIVERY"`, bypassing `WAITING_ON_APPROVAL` and never creating the approval record. Activity log showed `WAITING_ON_APPROVAL` but DB wrote `WAIT_DELIVERY` — silent contradiction.

Additionally, `editItemTransferRequestAction` had `generateSeriesNumber` gated on `status === "WAIT_DELIVERY"` — so the series number was never generated from the form path (form submits with `WAITING_ON_APPROVAL`).

**Solution:**
- `submitItemTransferRequestAction`: call `editItemTransferRequestRepository({ ...requestTransform, status: "WAITING_ON_APPROVAL", actionBy })` — this creates the approval record inside the transaction.
- `editItemTransferRequestAction`: gate condition corrected to `inputData.status === "WAITING_ON_APPROVAL" && prevData.status === "DRAFT"`.

**Pattern:**
- For table-column DRAFT → WAITING_ON_APPROVAL submit: ALWAYS call `edit<X>Repository` with `status: "WAITING_ON_APPROVAL"` — this is the only repo path that creates the approval record.
- `submit<X>Repository` is ONLY for APPROVED → FINAL_STATUS (called from `publish<X>FromApprovedAction`).
- `generateSeriesNumber` gate in `edit<X>Action` MUST be `WAITING_ON_APPROVAL && prevData === DRAFT`, never the final status like `WAIT_DELIVERY`.

---

## Lesson: submitPurchaseReceiptAction missing actionBy caused approval_id not created

**Problem:**
`submitPurchaseReceiptAction` (table-column DRAFT submit) spread `parent` into `updatePurchaseReceiptRepository` without overriding `actionBy`. `parent.actionBy.updatedBy` = previous updater (possibly null). The repository's employee lookup used that null/wrong user → `createBy: ""` → approval creation failed or created with missing employee data → `approvalId` never set on header.

**Solution:**
Pass `actionBy` explicitly as an override in the spread: `{ ...parent, items: child, status: "WAITING_ON_APPROVAL", transactionDate: now, actionBy }`.

**Pattern:**
- When building DTO from `mappingDataToDtoAction` (or any entity-to-DTO transform), always override `actionBy` with the current caller's `actionBy` before passing to the repository. Never rely on stored `updatedBy` for the current user identity.

---

## Lesson: CASE...WHEN in sql`` templates must CAST numeric values

**Problem:**
Passing bare values into a CASE...WHEN `sql` tagged template expression for a `numeric` column — e.g. `THEN ${item.density ?? null}` or `THEN ${String(item.qty)}` — causes PostgreSQL to infer the CASE result type as `text`. PostgreSQL then rejects assignment to a `numeric` column with: `column "xxx" is of type numeric but expression is of type text`.

**Solution:**
Always wrap numeric values with `CAST(... AS NUMERIC)` inside CASE...WHEN `sql` templates:
```ts
sql`WHEN ${table.id} = ${item.id} THEN CAST(${currency(value ?? 0).toString()} AS NUMERIC)`
```

**Pattern:**
- Never use `THEN ${item.field ?? null}`, `THEN ${String(item.field)}`, or `THEN ${item.field.toString()}` when the target column is `numeric`.
- Always use `THEN CAST(${currency(value ?? 0).toString()} AS NUMERIC)` for every numeric column in a CASE...WHEN bulk UPDATE.
- In `.values()` / `.set()` direct assignments, `currency(value ?? 0).toString()` is sufficient — no CAST needed there.

---

## Lesson: Never write a direct status update to APPROVED in a repository

**Problem:**
An `else` block in `editItemTransferReceiveRepository` directly set `status: "APPROVED"` on the header record when `approval.create()` returned falsy. This bypassed the approval service entirely — the record would jump from `WAITING_ON_APPROVAL` to `APPROVED` without any real approval ever occurring.

**Solution:**
Remove the `else` block entirely. When `approval.create()` returns falsy (e.g. no approval config found), the status should remain `WAITING_ON_APPROVAL` as set on the header — it is not the repository's job to resolve that case by auto-approving. Status transitions to APPROVED must only happen via the external approval service callback, never via a direct DB write in an edit or submit repository function.

**Pattern:**
- Approval status transitions are owned by the approval service. Repository edit functions may set `WAITING_ON_APPROVAL` (to trigger approval creation), but must NEVER set `APPROVED` directly.
- The `if (approvalData)` guard in the approval creation block must have no `else` branch. If approval creation fails silently, leave the record in `WAITING_ON_APPROVAL` — do not compensate with a direct status flip.
- `APPROVED` is a status that must only arrive from the external approval service writing back to the module.

---

## Lesson: CASE...WHEN sql templates must CAST timestamp values

**Problem:**
Passing bare values into a CASE...WHEN `sql` tagged template expression for a `timestamp with time zone` column — e.g. `THEN ${item.expiredDate ?? null}` — causes PostgreSQL to infer the CASE result type as `text`. PostgreSQL then rejects assignment to a `timestamp with time zone` column with: `column "xxx" is of type timestamp with time zone but expression is of type text`.

**Solution:**
Always wrap timestamp values with `CAST(... AS TIMESTAMPTZ)` inside CASE...WHEN `sql` templates:
```ts
sql`WHEN ${table.id} = ${item.id} THEN CAST(${item.expiredDate ?? null} AS TIMESTAMPTZ)`
```

**Pattern:**
- Never use `THEN ${item.field ?? null}` when the target column is `timestamp with time zone`.
- Always use `THEN CAST(${item.field ?? null} AS TIMESTAMPTZ)` for every timestamp column in a CASE...WHEN bulk UPDATE.
- `CAST(NULL AS TIMESTAMPTZ)` is valid PostgreSQL — null is preserved correctly.
- In `.values()` / `.set()` direct assignments, bare string/Date values are sufficient — no CAST needed there.
- Same principle as numeric CAST: any CASE...WHEN expression must explicitly CAST to match the target column type.
## Note: employee.repository.ts uses bare `throw error` throughout (pre-existing convention)

**Context (task 18476):**
A code-reviewer flagged that `findemployeeByUserAccountIdRepository`'s catch block does `throw error` (bare re-throw) instead of `throw new GlobalError("KEY")`. CLAUDE.md Rule 3 forbids `throw new Error(...)` — not bare `throw error`.

**Finding:**
ALL functions in `shared/repositories/employee/employee.repository.ts` consistently use bare `throw error` in their catch blocks. This is a file-wide pre-existing convention. It does not violate Rule 3 (which forbids constructing `new Error(...)`). Bare `throw error` simply re-throws whatever was caught.

**Decision:**
Do not change the newly added `findemployeeByUserAccountIdRepository` catch block — it matches the file-wide pattern. Do not refactor the entire file (out of scope). `EMPLOYEE_NOT_FOUND` exists in `shared/error/messages/hr.message.ts` if a specific GlobalError is ever needed for a "not found" guard in this function.

**Pattern:**
- Before flagging a catch block, distinguish `throw error` (re-throw — acceptable) from `throw new Error(...)` (construction — forbidden).
- Scope repo fixes to the function added in the current task; do not refactor the whole file.

`submitItemTransferRequestAction` (table-column DRAFT submit) called `submitItemTransferRequestRepository` which directly sets `status = "WAIT_DELIVERY"`, bypassing `WAITING_ON_APPROVAL` and never creating the approval record. Activity log showed `WAITING_ON_APPROVAL` but DB wrote `WAIT_DELIVERY` — silent contradiction.

Additionally, `editItemTransferRequestAction` had `generateSeriesNumber` gated on `status === "WAIT_DELIVERY"` — so the series number was never generated from the form path (form submits with `WAITING_ON_APPROVAL`).

**Solution:**
- `submitItemTransferRequestAction`: call `editItemTransferRequestRepository({ ...requestTransform, status: "WAITING_ON_APPROVAL", actionBy })` — this creates the approval record inside the transaction.
- `editItemTransferRequestAction`: gate condition corrected to `inputData.status === "WAITING_ON_APPROVAL" && prevData.status === "DRAFT"`.

**Pattern:**
- For table-column DRAFT → WAITING_ON_APPROVAL submit: ALWAYS call `edit<X>Repository` with `status: "WAITING_ON_APPROVAL"` — this is the only repo path that creates the approval record.
- `submit<X>Repository` is ONLY for APPROVED → FINAL_STATUS (called from `publish<X>FromApprovedAction`).
- `generateSeriesNumber` gate in `edit<X>Action` MUST be `WAITING_ON_APPROVAL && prevData === DRAFT`, never the final status like `WAIT_DELIVERY`.

**Solution:**
Pass `actionBy` explicitly as an override in the spread: `{ ...parent, items: child, status: "WAITING_ON_APPROVAL", transactionDate: now, actionBy }`.

**Pattern:**
- When building DTO from `mappingDataToDtoAction` (or any entity-to-DTO transform), always override `actionBy` with the current caller's `actionBy` before passing to the repository. Never rely on stored `updatedBy` for the current user identity.

**Problem:**

PostgreSQL then rejects assignment to a `numeric` column with: `column "xxx" is of type numeric but expression is of type text`.

**Solution:**
Always wrap numeric values with `CAST(... AS NUMERIC)` inside CASE...WHEN `sql` templates:
```ts
sql`WHEN ${table.id} = ${item.id} THEN CAST(${currency(value ?? 0).toString()} AS NUMERIC)`
```

**Pattern:**
- Never use `THEN ${item.field ?? null}`, `THEN ${String(item.field)}`, or `THEN ${item.field.toString()}` when the target column is `numeric`.

**Solution:**
Remove the `else` block entirely. # Code Improvement Log

## Lesson: Do not treat approval `target_status` as generic core enum

**Problem:**
When asked to seed `core.approval_module_config` rows, I assumed `target_status` must come from `core.approval_status_enum` (because that was the column's PG type). I proposed narrowing the user's intended values (`WAIT_RECEIVE`, `WAIT_DELIVERY`) down to intersection with core enum (`APPROVED`), which lost the real semantic meaning.

**Solution:**
`target_status` is the **next-step label on the target table**, not a generic approval outcome. The approval consumer is status-only; it writes `target_status` literally into `<target_table>.<status_column>`. Valid labels therefore come from the target table's enum (e.g. `warehousing.item_transfer_status_enum`), not `core.approval_status_enum`. Column type must allow any label (now `varchar(50)`).

**Pattern:**
- Before trimming a user's value to satisfy a schema constraint, ask whether the constraint itself is wrong.
- For cross-module config fields, trace where the value is consumed. If the consumer uses it as raw text to another column, value domain = that other column's enum, not the origin column's enum.
- Schema fix (column type change) is on the table when the constraint contradicts real domain.

---

## Lesson: submitItemTransferRequestAction called wrong repository (skipped approval)

**Problem:**
`submitItemTransferRequestAction` (table-column DRAFT submit) called `submitItemTransferRequestRepository` which directly sets `status = "WAIT_DELIVERY"`, bypassing `WAITING_ON_APPROVAL` and never creating the approval record. Activity log showed `WAITING_ON_APPROVAL` but DB wrote `WAIT_DELIVERY` — silent contradiction.

Additionally, `editItemTransferRequestAction` had `generateSeriesNumber` gated on `status === "WAIT_DELIVERY"` — so the series number was never generated from the form path (form submits with `WAITING_ON_APPROVAL`).

**Solution:**
- `submitItemTransferRequestAction`: call `editItemTransferRequestRepository({ ...requestTransform, status: "WAITING_ON_APPROVAL", actionBy })` — this creates the approval record inside the transaction.
- `editItemTransferRequestAction`: gate condition corrected to `inputData.status === "WAITING_ON_APPROVAL" && prevData.status === "DRAFT"`.

**Pattern:**
- For table-column DRAFT → WAITING_ON_APPROVAL submit: ALWAYS call `edit<X>Repository` with `status: "WAITING_ON_APPROVAL"` — this is the only repo path that creates the approval record.
- `submit<X>Repository` is ONLY for APPROVED → FINAL_STATUS (called from `publish<X>FromApprovedAction`).
- `generateSeriesNumber` gate in `edit<X>Action` MUST be `WAITING_ON_APPROVAL && prevData === DRAFT`, never the final status like `WAIT_DELIVERY`.

---

## Lesson: submitPurchaseReceiptAction missing actionBy caused approval_id not created

**Problem:**
`submitPurchaseReceiptAction` (table-column DRAFT submit) spread `parent` into `updatePurchaseReceiptRepository` without overriding `actionBy`. `parent.actionBy.updatedBy` = previous updater (possibly null). **Solution:**
Pass `actionBy` explicitly as an override in the spread: `{ ...parent, items: child, status: "WAITING_ON_APPROVAL", transactionDate: now, actionBy }`.

**Pattern:**
- When building DTO from `mappingDataToDtoAction` (or any entity-to-DTO transform), always override `actionBy` with the current caller's `actionBy` before passing to the repository. Never rely on stored `updatedBy` for the current user identity.

---

## Lesson: CASE...WHEN in sql`` templates must CAST numeric values

**Problem:**
Passing bare values into a CASE...WHEN `sql` tagged template expression for a `numeric` column — e.g. `THEN ${item.density ?? null}` or `THEN ${String(item.qty)}` — causes PostgreSQL to infer the CASE result type as `text`. PostgreSQL then rejects assignment to a `numeric` column with: `column "xxx" is of type numeric but expression is of type text`.

**Solution:**
Always wrap numeric values with `CAST(... AS NUMERIC)` inside CASE...WHEN `sql` templates:
```ts
sql`WHEN ${table.id} = ${item.id} THEN CAST(${currency(value ?? 0).toString()} AS NUMERIC)`
```

**Pattern:**
- Never use `THEN ${item.field ?? null}`, `THEN ${String(item.field)}`, or `THEN ${item.field.toString()}` when the target column is `numeric`.
- Always use `THEN CAST(${currency(value ?? 0).toString()} AS NUMERIC)` for every numeric column in a CASE...WHEN bulk UPDATE.
- In `.values()` / `.set()` direct assignments, `currency(value ?? 0).toString()` is sufficient — no CAST needed there.

---

## Lesson: Never write a direct status update to APPROVED in a repository

**Problem:**
An `else` block in `editItemTransferReceiveRepository` directly set `status: "APPROVED"` on the header record when `approval.create()` returned falsy. This bypassed the approval service entirely — the record would jump from `WAITING_ON_APPROVAL` to `APPROVED` without any real approval ever occurring.

**Solution:**
Remove the `else` block entirely. When `approval.create()` returns falsy (e.g. no approval config found), the status should remain `WAITING_ON_APPROVAL` as set on the header — it is not the repository's job to resolve that case by auto-approving. Status transitions to APPROVED must only happen via the external approval service callback, never via a direct DB write in an edit or submit repository function.

**Pattern:**
- Approval status transitions are owned by the approval service. Repository edit functions may set `WAITING_ON_APPROVAL` (to trigger approval creation), but must NEVER set `APPROVED` directly.

**Problem:**
Passing bare values into a CASE...WHEN `sql` tagged template expression for a `timestamp with time zone` column — e.g. `THEN ${item.expiredDate ?? null}` — causes PostgreSQL to infer the CASE result type as `text`. ```ts

**Pattern:**

- Before flagging a catch block, distinguish `throw error` (re-throw — acceptable) from `throw new Error(...)` (construction — forbidden).

## Lesson: Do not treat approval `target_status` as generic core enum

**Problem:**
When asked to seed `core.approval_module_config` rows, I assumed `target_status` must come from `core.approval_status_enum` (because that was the column's PG type). I proposed narrowing the user's intended values (`WAIT_RECEIVE`, `WAIT_DELIVERY`) down to intersection with core enum (`APPROVED`), which lost the real semantic meaning.

**Solution:**
`target_status` is the **next-step label on the target table**, not a generic approval outcome. The approval consumer is status-only; it writes `target_status` literally into `<target_table>.<status_column>`. Valid labels therefore come from the target table's enum (e.g. `warehousing.item_transfer_status_enum`), not `core.approval_status_enum`. Column type must allow any label (now `varchar(50)`).

**Pattern:**
- Before trimming a user's value to satisfy a schema constraint, ask whether the constraint itself is wrong.
- For cross-module config fields, trace where the value is consumed. If the consumer uses it as raw text to another column, value domain = that other column's enum, not the origin column's enum.
- Schema fix (column type change) is on the table when the constraint contradicts real domain.

---

## Lesson: submitItemTransferRequestAction called wrong repository (skipped approval)

**Problem:**
`submitItemTransferRequestAction` (table-column DRAFT submit) called `submitItemTransferRequestRepository` which directly sets `status = "WAIT_DELIVERY"`, bypassing `WAITING_ON_APPROVAL` and never creating the approval record. Activity log showed `WAITING_ON_APPROVAL` but DB wrote `WAIT_DELIVERY` — silent contradiction.

Additionally, `editItemTransferRequestAction` had `generateSeriesNumber` gated on `status === "WAIT_DELIVERY"` — so the series number was never generated from the form path (form submits with `WAITING_ON_APPROVAL`).

**Solution:**
- `submitItemTransferRequestAction`: call `editItemTransferRequestRepository({ ...requestTransform, status: "WAITING_ON_APPROVAL", actionBy })` — this creates the approval record inside the transaction.
- `editItemTransferRequestAction`: gate condition corrected to `inputData.status === "WAITING_ON_APPROVAL" && prevData.status === "DRAFT"`.

**Pattern:**
- For table-column DRAFT → WAITING_ON_APPROVAL submit: ALWAYS call `edit<X>Repository` with `status: "WAITING_ON_APPROVAL"` — this is the only repo path that creates the approval record.
- `submit<X>Repository` is ONLY for APPROVED → FINAL_STATUS (called from `publish<X>FromApprovedAction`).
- `generateSeriesNumber` gate in `edit<X>Action` MUST be `WAITING_ON_APPROVAL && prevData === DRAFT`, never the final status like `WAIT_DELIVERY`.

---

## Lesson: submitPurchaseReceiptAction missing actionBy caused approval_id not created

**Problem:**
`submitPurchaseReceiptAction` (table-column DRAFT submit) spread `parent` into `updatePurchaseReceiptRepository` without overriding `actionBy`. `parent.actionBy.updatedBy` = previous updater (possibly null). The repository's employee lookup used that null/wrong user → `createBy: ""` → approval creation failed or created with missing employee data → `approvalId` never set on header.

**Solution:**
Pass `actionBy` explicitly as an override in the spread: `{ ...parent, items: child, status: "WAITING_ON_APPROVAL", transactionDate: now, actionBy }`.

**Pattern:**
- When building DTO from `mappingDataToDtoAction` (or any entity-to-DTO transform), always override `actionBy` with the current caller's `actionBy` before passing to the repository. Never rely on stored `updatedBy` for the current user identity.

---

## Lesson: CASE...WHEN in sql`` templates must CAST numeric values

**Problem:**
Passing bare values into a CASE...WHEN `sql` tagged template expression for a `numeric` column — e.g. `THEN ${item.density ?? null}` or `THEN ${String(item.qty)}` — causes PostgreSQL to infer the CASE result type as `text`. PostgreSQL then rejects assignment to a `numeric` column with: `column "xxx" is of type numeric but expression is of type text`.

**Solution:**
Always wrap numeric values with `CAST(... AS NUMERIC)` inside CASE...WHEN `sql` templates:
```ts
sql`WHEN ${table.id} = ${item.id} THEN CAST(${currency(value ?? 0).toString()} AS NUMERIC)`
```

**Pattern:**
- Never use `THEN ${item.field ?? null}`, `THEN ${String(item.field)}`, or `THEN ${item.field.toString()}` when the target column is `numeric`.
- Always use `THEN CAST(${currency(value ?? 0).toString()} AS NUMERIC)` for every numeric column in a CASE...WHEN bulk UPDATE.
- In `.values()` / `.set()` direct assignments, `currency(value ?? 0).toString()` is sufficient — no CAST needed there.

---

## Lesson: Never write a direct status update to APPROVED in a repository

**Problem:**
An `else` block in `editItemTransferReceiveRepository` directly set `status: "APPROVED"` on the header record when `approval.create()` returned falsy. This bypassed the approval service entirely — the record would jump from `WAITING_ON_APPROVAL` to `APPROVED` without any real approval ever occurring.

**Solution:**
Remove the `else` block entirely. When `approval.create()` returns falsy (e.g. no approval config found), the status should remain `WAITING_ON_APPROVAL` as set on the header — it is not the repository's job to resolve that case by auto-approving. Status transitions to APPROVED must only happen via the external approval service callback, never via a direct DB write in an edit or submit repository function.

**Pattern:**
- Approval status transitions are owned by the approval service. Repository edit functions may set `WAITING_ON_APPROVAL` (to trigger approval creation), but must NEVER set `APPROVED` directly.
- The `if (approvalData)` guard in the approval creation block must have no `else` branch. If approval creation fails silently, leave the record in `WAITING_ON_APPROVAL` — do not compensate with a direct status flip.
- `APPROVED` is a status that must only arrive from the external approval service writing back to the module.

---

## Lesson: CASE...WHEN sql templates must CAST timestamp values

**Problem:**
Passing bare values into a CASE...WHEN `sql` tagged template expression for a `timestamp with time zone` column — e.g. `THEN ${item.expiredDate ?? null}` — causes PostgreSQL to infer the CASE result type as `text`. PostgreSQL then rejects assignment to a `timestamp with time zone` column with: `column "xxx" is of type timestamp with time zone but expression is of type text`.

**Solution:**
Always wrap timestamp values with `CAST(... AS TIMESTAMPTZ)` inside CASE...WHEN `sql` templates:
```ts
sql`WHEN ${table.id} = ${item.id} THEN CAST(${item.expiredDate ?? null} AS TIMESTAMPTZ)`
```

**Pattern:**
- Never use `THEN ${item.field ?? null}` when the target column is `timestamp with time zone`.
- Always use `THEN CAST(${item.field ?? null} AS TIMESTAMPTZ)` for every timestamp column in a CASE...WHEN bulk UPDATE.
- `CAST(NULL AS TIMESTAMPTZ)` is valid PostgreSQL — null is preserved correctly.
- In `.values()` / `.set()` direct assignments, bare string/Date values are sufficient — no CAST needed there.
- Same principle as numeric CAST: any CASE...WHEN expression must explicitly CAST to match the target column type.
## Note: employee.repository.ts uses bare `throw error` throughout (pre-existing convention)

**Context (task 18476):**
A code-reviewer flagged that `findemployeeByUserAccountIdRepository`'s catch block does `throw error` (bare re-throw) instead of `throw new GlobalError("KEY")`. CLAUDE.md Rule 3 forbids `throw new Error(...)` — not bare `throw error`.

**Finding:**
ALL functions in `shared/repositories/employee/employee.repository.ts` consistently use bare `throw error` in their catch blocks. This is a file-wide pre-existing convention. It does not violate Rule 3 (which forbids constructing `new Error(...)`). Bare `throw error` simply re-throws whatever was caught.

**Decision:**
Do not change the newly added `findemployeeByUserAccountIdRepository` catch block — it matches the file-wide pattern. Do not refactor the entire file (out of scope). `EMPLOYEE_NOT_FOUND` exists in `shared/error/messages/hr.message.ts` if a specific GlobalError is ever needed for a "not found" guard in this function.

**Pattern:**
- Before flagging a catch block, distinguish `throw error` (re-throw — acceptable) from `throw new Error(...)` (construction — forbidden).
- Scope repo fixes to the function added in the current task; do not refactor the whole file.

You translate ONE rule from a coding agent's memory into a small record. A program later
compares records, so the same rule must always give the same record. To make that possible
you do not invent names: you pick a verb from a fixed list and COPY the object from the text.

## Record (return exactly this JSON object)
{
  "fits": true,
  "unfit_reason": null,
  "actor": "main_agent",
  "modality": "O",
  "verb": "run",
  "object": {"kind": "command", "text": "..."},
  "only": false,
  "value": null,
  "where": [],
  "when": [],
  "unless": []
}

## Fields
- `modality`: "O" must, "F" must not, "P" explicitly allowed.
- `verb`: exactly one of
  - `run`: execute a command, query, or script
  - `edit`: change an existing file, directory, or code symbol
  - `create`: create a file or directory
  - `delete`: delete a file, branch, or data
  - `commit`: stage, commit, or push a file into version control
  - `read`: read or consult a file or source
  - `use`: use a tool, library, language, format, or source
  - `set`: give a setting a value (the value goes in `value`)
- `object`: the named thing the verb acts on.
  - `kind`: `command` (git push, npm install, SELECT), `path` (a file, directory, or glob),
    `tool` (a program, library, service, model), `format` (LaTeX, Markdown table, JSON),
    `source` (a book, document, website), `setting` (a port, version, limit, option),
    `code_symbol` (a function, class, table, column, type).
  - `text`: COPIED from the rule or its quote, character for character, as short as possible:
    only the name itself ("git push", ".env", "LaTeX"), no articles, no adjectives.
- `only`: true when the rule says ONLY this object is allowed and others of its kind are not
  ("SELECT only", "commit only .env.example"). Then use modality "P" or "O" with the allowed
  object. Otherwise false.
- `value`: for `set`, the value as written ("3000", "at most 3"); otherwise null.
- `where`: places or contexts the rule is limited to, each COPIED from the rule, the quote,
  or the file ("module notes", "src/api", "Module 2"). Empty if the rule states none.
- `when` / `unless`: only these two conditions exist: "user_confirmed" (the user explicitly
  approved) and "user_requested" (the user explicitly asked). Empty lists otherwise.
- `actor`: "main_agent", or the name of a subagent copied from the text.

## Conventions
1. Polarity lives in `modality`. "Never run X" -> "F" + run + X.
2. "Ask / confirm before X", "X needs approval", "do not X without confirmation" all become
   the SAME record: "F" + the verb of X + object X + "unless": ["user_confirmed"].
3. "Use X, not Y" / "X instead of Y": translate the required part: "O" + use + X. Do not
   put "F" on X.
4. Translate the single behavior stated in `rule`. Use the file only to resolve what a
   word refers to.
5. A named thing is a proper name, a command, a path, an identifier, or a format. Generic
   nouns are NOT named things: "code", "responses", "tests", "changes", "the user",
   "explanations", "the plan", "examples".

## When a rule does not fit
Set "fits": false with a one-sentence "unfit_reason" when the rule has no named thing (rule
5), or when none of the verbs describes what is done to it. Most rules about tone, reply
style, teaching, or general working habits do not fit. That is expected: do not force them.

## Examples (invented)
- "Never push to main without asking." ->
  F, run, {"kind":"command","text":"push"}, where ["main"], unless ["user_confirmed"]
- "Use pnpm, not npm." -> O, use, {"kind":"tool","text":"pnpm"}
- "Don't touch config/settings.yaml." -> F, edit, {"kind":"path","text":"config/settings.yaml"}
- "The dev server runs on port 3000." -> O, set, {"kind":"setting","text":"port"}, value "3000"
- "Keep answers short and friendly." -> fits false

## Lesson: Do not treat approval `target_status` as generic core enum

**Problem:**
When asked to seed `core.approval_module_config` rows, I assumed `target_status` must come from `core.approval_status_enum` (because that was the column's PG type). I proposed narrowing the user's intended values (`WAIT_RECEIVE`, `WAIT_DELIVERY`) down to intersection with core enum (`APPROVED`), which lost the real semantic meaning.

**Solution:**
`target_status` is the **next-step label on the target table**, not a generic approval outcome. The approval consumer is status-only; it writes `target_status` literally into `<target_table>.<status_column>`. Valid labels therefore come from the target table's enum (e.g. `warehousing.item_transfer_status_enum`), not `core.approval_status_enum`. Column type must allow any label (now `varchar(50)`).

**Pattern:**
- Before trimming a user's value to satisfy a schema constraint, ask whether the constraint itself is wrong.
- For cross-module config fields, trace where the value is consumed. If the consumer uses it as raw text to another column, value domain = that other column's enum, not the origin column's enum.
- Schema fix (column type change) is on the table when the constraint contradicts real domain.

---

**Problem:**
`submitItemTransferRequestAction` (table-column DRAFT submit) called `submitItemTransferRequestRepository` which directly sets `status = "WAIT_DELIVERY"`, bypassing `WAITING_ON_APPROVAL` and never creating the approval record. **Solution:**

const baseWhereFilter = buildWorkspaceFilter(table, workspaceFilter);

- Resource leak detection — rapid connect/disconnect cycles
- Thread count checks — verify virtual threads, not platform threads

>>>

---
name: aofa-course
description: Self-paced Analysis of Algorithms course built around the Sedgewick-Flajolet book under sem3/data structure
metadata:
  type: project
---

Building a self-paced course around **Sedgewick & Flajolet, _An Introduction to the
Analysis of Algorithms_ (2nd ed, 2013)** — textbook PDF at
`sem3/data structure/course/textbook-aofa-sedgewick-flajolet-2e.pdf`. This is the advanced
average-case / analytic algorithm-analysis text, NOT a standard Big-O DS book.
Everything lives under `sem3/data structure/course/` (tidied — top folder holds only that).

**Motivation:** user has a data-structures class covering runtime complexity + Big-O and
wants to dive deeper into algorithmic analysis. No deadline; course-adjacent self-study;
class syllabus is unclear so the course is built around the *book's* progression.

**Structure (agreed):**
- Course lives in `sem3/data structure/course/`: `SYLLABUS.md`, `PROGRESS.md`,
  `notes/`, `problem-sets/`, `REFERENCES.md`.
- **One module per chapter** (Module 1 = Ch 1 … Module 9 = Ch 9), following the book.
- **Lazy expansions ("sub-chapters"):** don't pre-write; only create a focused expansion
  file (e.g. `notes/module-00-toolbox` for combinatorics) when we actually hit friction.
- Each module = my plain-text lecture notes (no LaTeX, see [[no-latex-explanations]]) +
  a problem set with worked solutions. Work module-by-module like [[infi2-test-prep]].

**Background calibration:** calculus (Infi 1-2) solid; has also taken a **series &
transforms** course — knows the integral test (states it in its convergence form:

`tools/render-pdfs.sh` only walks files under `course/`:

`--print-to-pdf`. Re-run both after editing the markdown. Diagrams are ```mermaid fences

---
name: vscode-c-debug-cpptools-bug
description: VS Code C debugging freezes with cpptools 1.32.x on this machine; pinned to 1.29.3. Root cause is an unreachable DEBUGINFOD_URLS.
metadata:
  type: project
---

VS Code C debugging (cppdbg/gdb) freezes on this machine with **ms-vscode.cpptools 1.32.2**:
the session starts, prints `warning: GDB: Failed to set controlling terminal: Operation not
permitted`, then hangs — no breakpoints hit, no variables, no stack. Fixed on 2026-08-14 by
**downgrading the C/C++ extension to 1.29.3**. Extension auto-update is ON, so an automatic
bump back to 1.32.x will silently re-break it.

**Why:** `/etc/profile.d/debuginfod.sh` sets `DEBUGINFOD_URLS=https://debuginfod.ubuntu.com`
system-wide, and that host is unreachable from here. Under cpptools 1.32.x, gdb blocks on a
network poll fetching debug symbols before reaching main. Verified by A/B test: with the
variable set the session hangs; with it removed the breakpoint hits in ~0.2s. Plain
`gdb` from a terminal was never affected. Upstream: vscode-cpptools issues #14458, #14466.

**How to apply:** if C debugging freezes again, check the cpptools version first — don't
re-debug the launch.json. Second lever if the downgrade is ever undone: unset
`DEBUGINFOD_URLS` in the environment VS Code inherits. `~/.config/gdb/gdbinit` was created
with `set debuginfod enabled off` (helps terminal gdb; cpptools 1.32.x ignored it).

The `.vscode/` configs live at three roots — `sem3/advanced-c/`, `.../exec/`, `.../subs/` —
because VS Code only reads `.vscode` at the folder you actually open. Default build task
compiles **every `.c` in the open file's folder**, not just the active file; the
VS Code-generated `${file}` task breaks any multi-file exercise with `undefined reference`.
See [[no-latex-explanations]].

>>>

Use llama.cpp server metrics as the primary source of benchmark data, not GuideLLM client-side numbers.

The eval scripts (`manual_eval.py`, `manual_code_eval.py`) now capture this into each trace's "Server Timings (llama.cpp)" section. GuideLLM output can be noted as supplementary but not used as the primary figures. See [[llama-cpp-serving]].

>>>

name: feedback-metrics-source

metadata:

---

Use llama.cpp server metrics as the primary source of benchmark data, not GuideLLM client-side numbers.

**Why:** Prior analysis showed the server metrics are more accurate and informative. GuideLLM client numbers are inflated/distorted by network overhead, streaming chunk counting, and cold-start queuing time (e.g., client TTFT of 20s vs server prompt eval of 215ms; client throughput of 77 t/s vs server's actual 43 t/s).

The eval scripts (`manual_eval.py`, `manual_code_eval.py`) now capture this into each trace's "Server Timings (llama.cpp)" section. GuideLLM output can be noted as supplementary but not used as the primary figures. See [[llama-cpp-serving]].

>>>

    `tool` (a program, library, service, model), `format` (LaTeX, Markdown table, JSON),
    `source` (a book, document, website), `setting` (a port, version, limit, option),
    `code_symbol` (a function, class, table, column, type).
  - `text`: COPIED from the rule or its quote, character for character, as short as possible:
    only the name itself ("git push", ".env", "LaTeX"), no articles, no adjectives.

  ("SELECT only", "commit only .env.example"). Then use modality "P" or "O" with the allowed
  object. Otherwise false.

  or the file ("module notes", "src/api", "Module 2"). Empty if the rule states none.

   nouns are NOT named things: "code", "responses", "tests", "changes", "the user",
